_comment: Decision-engine fixture v1: algorithm selection and track-specific performance (issue #3). Rules: docs/mining_system.md §6.4 (challenge-wide algorithm choice by adoption) and §6.5 (track-specific qualifier rate, best-on-track). Adoption values are PreciseNumber decimal strings exactly as in fixtures/tig/v1/get-algorithms.json block_data.adoption. algorithm_track_stats maps derive from get-algorithms num_qualifiers_by_track_by_player (summed over players) and get-tracks-data num_bundles; see README.md. Tie direction (smallest algorithm_id wins) is a recorded convention, see README open question 2.

cases.name: highest_adoption_wins
cases.description: Three eligible algorithms; the one with the highest challenge-wide adoption is selected.
cases.rule: mining_system.md §6.4 step 3: 'select the algorithm with the highest current challenge-wide adoption'.

cases.name: zero_adoption_ignored
cases.description: An algorithm with zero challenge-wide adoption is ignored even though it is active with a usable binary; the only positive-adoption algorithm wins.
cases.rule: mining_system.md §6.4 step 2: 'ignore algorithms whose current challenge-wide adoption is zero'.

cases.name: all_zero_adoption_challenge_ineligible
cases.description: Every otherwise-usable algorithm has zero adoption, so no algorithm can be selected and the challenge has no eligible algorithm, making it ineligible for challenge selection.
cases.rule: mining_system.md §6.4 step 2 leaves no candidate; §6.2: 'A challenge is eligible only when the pool can construct valid settings for every active track using an eligible algorithm'.

cases.name: banned_and_missing_binary_filtered_before_adoption
cases.description: The two highest-adoption algorithms are excluded (one banned, one without a usable successful binary); the remaining clean algorithm is selected despite lower adoption.
cases.rule: mining_system.md §6.4 step 1: 'keep active, non-banned algorithms with a usable successful binary' — filtering precedes the adoption comparison in step 3.

cases.name: adoption_tie_resolved_by_algorithm_id
cases.description: Two algorithms tie on adoption; the tie is resolved deterministically by algorithm_id — the smallest id wins (recorded convention, README open question 2).
cases.rule: mining_system.md §6.4 step 4: 'resolve equal adoption deterministically by algorithm_id'. The direction (lexicographically smallest id wins) is a recorded fixture convention because §6.4 does not state it.

cases.name: track_best_by_highest_rate_does_not_change_selection
cases.description: a201 wins challenge-wide selection by adoption, but a202 has the higher qualifier rate on track t1 and is best on that track. The track-best result does not change the selected algorithm; it only feeds the CPU bundle-count rule.
cases.rule: mining_system.md §6.5: track_qualifier_rate[a,t] = qualifiers[a,t] / active_bundles[a,t]; best on track = greatest available rate; 'This track-best result does not change the already selected challenge-wide algorithm.' §6.4 selects a201 by adoption.

cases.name: no_active_bundles_no_usable_rate
cases.description: On track t2 the algorithm a201 has no active bundles, so it has no usable rate and cannot be best; a202, with the only available rate, is best on the track.
cases.rule: mining_system.md §6.5: 'Algorithms with no active bundles on the track do not have a usable rate. An algorithm is best on the track when it has the greatest available rate.'

cases.name: no_algorithm_has_active_bundles_no_track_best
cases.description: No eligible algorithm has active bundles on track t9, so no algorithm has a usable rate and there is no best algorithm on that track. In particular the selected algorithm is not best on t9, which forces min_num_bundles on t9 for a CPU member (§6.7).
cases.rule: mining_system.md §6.5: algorithms without active bundles have no usable rate; with no available rate there is no best-on-track algorithm.

cases.name: track_rate_tie_resolved_by_algorithm_id
cases.description: Two algorithms have the same qualifier rate (1/2) on track t3 from different counts; the tie is resolved deterministically by algorithm_id — smallest id wins (recorded convention, README open question 2).
cases.rule: mining_system.md §6.5: 'Ties are resolved deterministically by algorithm_id.' Rates compare as exact ratios: 2/4 = 3/6.
